summary:
Our idea is to elaborate a book for preteens and school level education called “tales of space castaways” to bring children around the globe closer to the world of astronomy and space and explain concepts which might seem intimidating at a first glance to create a generation full of curiosity and the wish to explore what’s out there, as well as promoting reading as a habit.

Due to the fact that we are minors none of the team members can use their voice to create an audiobook, but because one of our main objectives is to make it as accessible and inclusive as possible, we are going to use Eleven labs as a substitute. This will allow us to include people who are not so keen on reading as well as boys and girls with blindness or visual impediments.

The book will consist of various stories or short chapters in which the objects themselves tell their stories, from their creation to their eventual abandonment, and showcasing the variety of the missions and tools which are currently in space, how they work, and their respective purposes.
Each object will have some sort of personality to create a more appealing and fun reading process, and we think that a great way to do so is to grow attached to these little characters and their quirks.

We’re going to summarise and adapt the hard concepts, without dumbing down the topics, to make the reading more interesting and comprehensible, taking into account their reading comprehension to create a light but educational reading experience.
details:
For this project we had to use diferent artistic mediums such as writing and drawing, we used the resources that NASA provided us with to create the first chapter, and Eleven labs to create a audiobook, which is pivotal for the inclusion of children with vision disabilities

This book has the purpouse of introducing young audiences to the field of space exploration, as well as promoting a healthy habit like reading, which is truly important for their reading comprehension and critical thinking skills as well as being a healthy habit to have.

Many kids around the world dream about space, but they think it's something they can only dream about, with this project we wish to encourage young minds to try their best and remember that if they work hard enough those dreams aren't as distant as they might seem.

Our main goals are to make the book as inclusive as we can, to inspire children to dream big and explore, and to have a light and fun reading process without dumbing down concepts too much.
